expect.matrix_note_contains: Status reflects the latest live evidence

provenance: M35 eval-first. Deployment run 2ce3e5c8 (2026-08-22) showed that a task with no start URL spent a run guaranteed to fail, so this rendered case pins the no-URL guard, site-name URL inference, verified access-key header, and Try-button behavior. User report, 2026-08-30, narrowed the interview surface to finance: the case pins SEC filing analysis first, followed by seven finance workflows, five useful columns, zero empty matrix cells, and each new site's exact URL and Try task. Watched red before each UI change: first the irrelevant rows and stale 10-K task, then the absence of the four new finance rows. Cold review then found two silent-success gaps; both watched red before repair: an all-dash showcased row rendered as supported, and the Intel button loaded a generic status question rather than explicitly asking the agent to select Intel, run extraction, and read the result. The access success state was then pinned to the green `enabled` class after the owner showed that grey `✓ Enabled` was visually weaker than the SEC extractor; watched red first with status_class `note`. A second user report required showcase URLs to start at each site's homepage and added a Chinese TAIFEX navigation task; the exact nine roots and Chinese task were pinned before the page changed. The deployment-backed homepage probe on build 3927366 then supplied the first status evidence for those roots: Bank of Canada and ECB were independently ground-truthed 3/3 successes, while CompaniesMarketCap and TAIFEX failed loudly. These three changed status expectations were watched red against the pre-probe matrix before its declarations and notes were updated. Live QA after merge found the section note still claiming homepage navigation had not been re-rated; matrix_note_contains pins the corrected claim and was watched red against that deployed wording.
